Directed / Undirected
description: A directed edge A → B permits travel from A to B. An undirected edge A — B permits travel in both directions.

title: Cyclic / Acyclic
description: A cycle returns to its start along a nonempty path without repeating other vertices. A tree is connected and acyclic.

title: Weighted / Unweighted
description: A weighted edge carries a cost. BFS minimizes edge count. Dijkstra minimizes total nonnegative cost.

title: Connected / Disconnected
description: In an undirected graph, one traversal reaches every vertex exactly when the graph is connected. Otherwise each fresh traversal discovers another component.

title: DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph)
description: A directed acyclic graph has a topological ordering. Draw A → C and B → C: both prerequisites must precede C.

title: Adjacency Matrix
description: Represent V vertices with a V × V table. Row u, column v records edge u → v. Testing one edge takes O(1), while storage takes O(V²).

title: Adjacency List
description: Store a list of outgoing neighbors per vertex. Enumerating neighbors costs O(outdegree), and the whole structure uses O(V+E) space.

title: Edge List
description: Store each edge as (source, destination, weight). Iterating edges is direct, which suits Bellman-Ford and sorting edges for Kruskal.

title: Union by Rank
description: Attach the lower-rank root beneath the higher-rank root. Increase rank only when joining two equal-rank roots.

title: Union by Size
description: Maintain component sizes at their roots. Attach the smaller component to the larger one and add their sizes.
